Letter of April 24, 1972, to the State Clearinghouse from Chief, Environmental Resources Division, Montana Department of Fish and Game.
Comment: The letter concurs in the need to preserve endangered species, but believes that the State can do a better job than the Federal Covernment.
Response: For further comment on this point as relevant to the proposed legislation, see our reply to comment of the State of Indiana.
Comment: Concern is expressed that emphasis in the Environmental statement is toward restriction of man's use of endangered species with only minor emphasis on habitat management.
Response: We acknowledge that there is emphasis on restriction of man's use of such species, but this is because more details are required in the text of the law to protect endangered species from humans than are necessary to legislate most other forms of management. We are confident that actual programs for most species will reflect habitat management.
Comment: The letter objects that the admonition to other Federal agencies requires that they seek to protect endangered species only insofar as is practical and consistent with the primary purposes of the agency.
Response: We agree with the concern expressed, but insistence that the purposes of this proposal dominate all other interests without a case by case judgment, will invite dismissal of the proposal altogether. We believe that the section, as written, provides adequate authority for the Secretary of the Interior to seek the assistance of any Federal agency on a case by case basis and, further and more important, it authorized that agency to use its authority to benefit an endangered species.
